cognitive_biases.name: Survivorship Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Focusing on visible winners while overlooking invisible failures.

cognitive_biases.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy
cognitive_biases.hint: Continuing an unprofitable endeavor merely because resources were already spent.

cognitive_biases.name: Anchoring Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Fixating disproportionately on the first piece of information received.

cognitive_biases.name: Dunning-Kruger Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Beginners overestimating competence while true experts underestimate theirs.

cognitive_biases.name: Fundamental Attribution Error
cognitive_biases.hint: Attributing others' mistakes to character flaws while excusing your own as situational.

cognitive_biases.name: Framing Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Drawing opposite conclusions from identical data based entirely on how it is presented.

cognitive_biases.name: Confirmation Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Searching only for evidence that validates preexisting convictions.

cognitive_biases.name: Status Quo Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Defaulting to existing routines even when better alternatives exist.

cognitive_biases.name: Curse of Knowledge
cognitive_biases.hint: Assuming others understand complex concepts simply because they are obvious to you.

cognitive_biases.name: Peak-End Rule
cognitive_biases.hint: Remembering an experience by its emotional peak and conclusion, not its duration.

cognitive_biases.name: Availability Heuristic
cognitive_biases.hint: Overestimating the frequency of events that come to mind quickly.

cognitive_biases.name: Hyperbolic Discounting
cognitive_biases.hint: Valuing immediate small gratification over vastly larger delayed rewards.

cognitive_biases.name: Pluralistic Ignorance
cognitive_biases.hint: Privately rejecting a norm while assuming everyone else accepts it.

cognitive_biases.name: Streetlight Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Searching for solutions where searching is easiest rather than where the solution actually is.

cognitive_biases.name: Hindsight Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Believing an unpredictable outcome was obvious and foreseeable all along.

cognitive_biases.name: Naive Realism
cognitive_biases.hint: Believing you see reality objectively, while those who disagree must be biased or uninformed.

cognitive_biases.name: Base Rate Neglect
cognitive_biases.hint: Ignoring statistical baseline probabilities in favor of compelling individual anecdotes.

cognitive_biases.name: Outcome Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Judging a decision's quality solely by its outcome rather than the quality of the process.

cognitive_biases.name: Loss Aversion
cognitive_biases.hint: Feeling the psychological pain of a loss roughly twice as intensely as the joy of equivalent gain.

cognitive_biases.name: Zero-Risk Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Overpaying to eliminate a small risk entirely rather than reducing a much larger overall risk.

cognitive_biases.name: Bandwagon Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Adopting beliefs simply because a growing crowd has already done so.

cognitive_biases.name: Decoy Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Changing preference between two options when a third, dominated option is introduced.

cognitive_biases.name: Negativity Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Giving disproportionate cognitive weight to negative events over positive ones.

cognitive_biases.name: IKEA Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Placing an irrationally high value on products or projects you helped assemble.

cognitive_biases.name: Blind Spot Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Recognizing cognitive biases easily in others while failing to notice them in yourself.

cognitive_biases.name: False Consensus Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Overestimating how many people share your personal beliefs and preferences.

cognitive_biases.name: Frequency Illusion (Baader-Meinhof)
cognitive_biases.hint: Noticing a recently learned word, thing, or concept everywhere you look.

cognitive_biases.name: Planning Fallacy
cognitive_biases.hint: Systematically underestimating the time, cost, and risk of future actions.

cognitive_biases.name: Egocentric Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Remembering and weighting your own contributions far more than the contributions of others.

cognitive_biases.name: Empathy Gap
cognitive_biases.hint: Underestimating the influence of visceral physical and emotional drives on future decision making.

cognitive_biases.name: Omission Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Judging harmful actions as worse than equally harmful failures to act.

cognitive_biases.name: Overconfidence Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Subjective confidence in judgments being reliably higher than objective accuracy.

cognitive_biases.name: Law of the Instrument (Maslow's Hammer)
cognitive_biases.hint: Over-relying on a familiar tool or framework to solve completely unsuitable problems.

cognitive_biases.name: Focusing Illusion
cognitive_biases.hint: Thinking nothing in life is as important as whatever you are currently thinking about.

cognitive_biases.name: Normalcy Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Underestimating the possibility and effect of a disaster because it hasn't happened before.

cognitive_biases.name: Projection Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Assuming your future self will have the exact same tastes and priorities as you do right now.

cognitive_biases.name: Self-Serving Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Claiming personal credit for successes while blaming external circumstances for failures.

cognitive_biases.name: Authority Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Attributing greater accuracy to the opinion of an authority figure regardless of substance.

cognitive_biases.name: Halo Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Allowing an initial positive impression in one trait to influence global judgments of character.

cognitive_biases.name: Choice-Supportive Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Retroactively attributing positive qualities to whichever option you previously selected.

cognitive_biases.name: Backfire Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Strengthening prior convictions when confronted with contradictory evidence.

cognitive_biases.name: Rhyme-as-Reason Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Judging statements as more truthful and accurate simply because they are formulated to rhyme.

cognitive_biases.name: Subadditivity Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Judging the probability of a whole as less than the sum of probabilities of its parts.

cognitive_biases.name: Effort Justification
cognitive_biases.hint: Overvaluing an outcome merely because attaining it required painful effort.

cognitive_biases.name: Social Proof Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Assuming surrounding individuals possess better knowledge about the correct course of action.

cognitive_biases.name: Survivorship of Metrics (Goodhart's Trap)
cognitive_biases.hint: Optimizing for easily recorded metrics while starving invisible core qualities.

cognitive_biases.name: Restraint Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Overestimating your ability to resist impulsive temptation when faced with it directly.

cognitive_biases.name: Distinction Bias
cognitive_biases.hint: Viewing two options as distinctive when evaluating them side-by-side, but identical in isolation.

cognitive_biases.name: Just-World Fallacy
cognitive_biases.hint: Assuming actions inevitably have morally fair and fitting consequences for the actor.

cognitive_biases.name: Third-Person Effect
cognitive_biases.hint: Believing mass media or advertising affects other people far more than it affects you.

neuroscience.name: Attention Residue
neuroscience.hint: Context-switching leaves neural focus trapped in the prior task for up to 20 minutes.

neuroscience.name: Optic Flow & Panoramic Vision
neuroscience.hint: Expanding peripheral vision down-regulates sympathetic fight-or-flight arousal in seconds.

neuroscience.name: Adenosine & Sleep Pressure
neuroscience.hint: Adenosine accumulates during waking hours, creating physical sleepiness that caffeine only masks.

neuroscience.name: Dopamine Reward Prediction Error
neuroscience.hint: Dopamine fires on the gap between anticipation and reality, not on the reward itself.

neuroscience.name: Ultradian Rhythms
neuroscience.hint: The brain operates in 90-minute ultradian cycles of focus followed by mandatory recovery troughs.

neuroscience.name: Default Mode Network
neuroscience.hint: Subconscious neural circuits synthesize disparate memories and solve complex problems during rest.

neuroscience.name: Cognitive Load & Working Memory Buffer
neuroscience.hint: Working memory holds roughly 4 chunks of active information before degradation occurs.

neuroscience.name: Spaced Repetition & Synaptic Consolidation
neuroscience.hint: Re-testing information right before it fades triggers long-term potentiation in synapses.

neuroscience.name: Physiological Sigh
neuroscience.hint: Two quick nasal inhales followed by a long, slow exhale rapidly slows heart rate via the vagus nerve.

neuroscience.name: Temperature Minimum & Circadian Reset
neuroscience.hint: Core body temperature hits its lowest point roughly 2 hours before natural waking.

neuroscience.name: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR)
neuroscience.hint: 20 minutes of shallow hypnotic relaxation restores striatal dopamine and cognitive stamina.

neuroscience.name: Visual Anchoring & Prefrontal Focus
neuroscience.hint: Restricting visual gaze to a single point primes prefrontal neural circuits for deep concentration.

neuroscience.name: Cortisol Awakening Response
neuroscience.hint: A healthy morning cortisol spike sets the internal clock for daytime alertness and nocturnal sleep.

neuroscience.name: Myelination & Deep Practice
neuroscience.hint: Repetitive, high-focus practice wraps neural axons in myelin, permanently accelerating electrical signaling.

neuroscience.name: State-Dependent Learning
neuroscience.hint: Information is recalled most accurately when the internal physiological state matches the learning state.

neuroscience.name: Error-Driven Neuroplasticity
neuroscience.hint: Experiencing friction and frustration triggers acetylcholine and epinephrine release, marking synapses for rewiring.

neuroscience.name: Melatonin Suppression from Blue Light
neuroscience.hint: Short-wavelength light strikes melanopsin retinal cells, shutting down pineal melatonin synthesis.

neuroscience.name: Dual-Task Interference
neuroscience.hint: The prefrontal cortex cannot process two conscious linguistic tasks simultaneously without massive error rates.

neuroscience.name: Stochastic Resonance
neuroscience.hint: Low levels of ambient pink or white noise can sharpen weak sensory signals in neural circuits.

neuroscience.name: Glymphatic Cleansing
neuroscience.hint: Cerebrospinal fluid flushes metabolic waste and amyloid beta from brain interstitial space during deep slow-wave sleep.

neuroscience.name: Reticular Activating System
neuroscience.hint: The brainstem gateway that filters millions of sensory inputs down to what you consciously care about.

neuroscience.name: Basal Ganglia Habit Offloading
neuroscience.hint: Repeated behaviors migrate from the costly prefrontal cortex into energy-efficient basal ganglia routines.

neuroscience.name: Testing Effect (Effortful Retrieval)
neuroscience.hint: Actively recalling an answer from memory strengthens neural pathways far more than re-reading notes.

neuroscience.name: Yerkes-Dodson Arousal Curve
neuroscience.hint: Cognitive performance peaks under moderate physiological arousal; too little causes sluggishness, too much causes panic.

neuroscience.name: Interoceptive Awareness
neuroscience.hint: The insular cortex processes internal bodily signals (heart rate, breathing) to inform intuitive decision-making.

neuroscience.name: BDNF from Aerobic Exercise
neuroscience.hint: Elevated heart rate triggers Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor release, stimulating hippocampal neurogenesis.

neuroscience.name: Anterior Cingulate Cortex & Tenacity
neuroscience.hint: Engaging in effortful tasks you do not want to do physically enlarges the anterior mid-cingulate cortex.

neuroscience.name: Foveal Tunneling vs Peripheral Gaze
neuroscience.hint: Narrow focal vision activates vigilance pathways, while broad peripheral vision activates parasympathetic calming.

neuroscience.name: Prospective Memory Offloading
neuroscience.hint: Writing down an unfinished task relieves working memory tension caused by the Zeigarnik effect.

neuroscience.name: Hippocampal Cognitive Maps
neuroscience.hint: Place and grid cells in the hippocampus build spatial navigation maps that double as conceptual memory frameworks.

neuroscience.name: Circadian Feeding Entrainment
neuroscience.hint: Peripheral clocks in the liver and gut sync to feeding timing, influencing midday energy crashes.

neuroscience.name: Cognitive Reappraisal
neuroscience.hint: Reinterpreting physiological arousal from 'anxiety' to 'excitement' down-regulates amygdala reactivity.

neuroscience.name: L-Theanine Alpha Waves
neuroscience.hint: Modulates glutamate receptors to promote calm, relaxed focus without inducing sedation.

neuroscience.name: Synaptic Pruning
neuroscience.hint: Microglia physically eliminate weak, unused synapses during deep sleep, keeping neural networks lean.

neuroscience.name: Mirror Neuron Empathy Circuits
neuroscience.hint: Motor and premotor neurons fire both when performing an action and when observing another perform it.

neuroscience.name: Neural Entrainment
neuroscience.hint: Brainwave frequencies naturally synchronize to repetitive external auditory or visual rhythms.

neuroscience.name: Anterior Mid-Insula Gut-Brain Axis
neuroscience.hint: Vagal afferent nerves transmit direct microbial and gastrointestinal signals into affective brain centers.

neuroscience.name: Dopamine Baseline Depletion
neuroscience.hint: Pursuing sharp, artificial dopamine spikes inevitably results in a temporary drop below your prior baseline.

neuroscience.name: Cold Shock Epinephrine Surge
neuroscience.hint: Brief cold water immersion triggers prolonged, sustained increases in circulating dopamine and epinephrine.

neuroscience.name: Cerebellar Prediction Engine
neuroscience.hint: The cerebellum continuously calculates sensory predictions, subtracting expected feedback so the brain focuses on novel anomalies.

neuroscience.name: Striatal Action Selection
neuroscience.hint: The dorsal striatum weighs competing motor commands, suppressing all actions except the chosen priority.

neuroscience.name: Olfactory Direct Limbic Pathway
neuroscience.hint: Smell bypasses the thalamus relay, routing directly into the amygdala and hippocampus for vivid memory recall.

neuroscience.name: Vocal Feedback Self-Monitoring
neuroscience.hint: Auditory cortex attenuates self-generated vocal sounds so you can detect external sounds while speaking.

neuroscience.name: Somatosensory Hand Map Plasticity
neuroscience.hint: The cortical area dedicated to fingers expands or contracts rapidly based on fine motor practice.

neuroscience.name: Circadian Melatonin Rebound
neuroscience.hint: Allowing eyes to register sunset light cues the suprachiasmatic nucleus to time natural nighttime melatonin release.

mental_models.name: Gall's Law
mental_models.hint: A complex system that works invariably evolved from a simple system that worked.

mental_models.name: Chesterton's Fence
mental_models.hint: Never remove a fence, rule, or piece of code until you understand why it was built in the first place.

mental_models.name: Second-Order Thinking
mental_models.hint: Always ask: 'And then what?' considering downstream secondary and tertiary consequences.

mental_models.name: Inversion (Jacobi / Stoic)
mental_models.hint: Instead of asking how to succeed, ask how to guarantee failure and systematically avoid those steps.

mental_models.name: First Principles Thinking
mental_models.hint: Boil a problem down to its foundational truths and reason up from there rather than by analogy.

mental_models.name: Lindy Effect
mental_models.hint: The future life expectancy of non-perishable ideas and technologies is proportional to their current age.

mental_models.name: Hanlon's Razor
mental_models.hint: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by carelessness or misunderstanding.

mental_models.name: Goodhart's Law
mental_models.hint: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a reliable measure.

mental_models.name: Occam's Razor
mental_models.hint: Among competing hypotheses that predict equally well, choose the one with the fewest assumptions.

mental_models.name: Circle of Competence
mental_models.hint: Knowing the precise boundary of what you truly understand versus what you only think you understand.

mental_models.name: Conway's Law
mental_models.hint: Organizations design systems that mirror their internal communication structures.

mental_models.name: Parkinson's Law
mental_models.hint: Work expands to fill the time allocated for its completion.

mental_models.name: The Map is Not the Territory
mental_models.hint: Models, abstractions, and specs are useful simplifications, not reality itself.

mental_models.name: The Cobra Effect
mental_models.hint: When an attempted incentive or solution makes the original problem worse through perverse incentives.

mental_models.name: Leaky Abstractions
mental_models.hint: All non-trivial abstractions leak details of the underlying implementation they attempt to hide.

mental_models.name: Hyrum's Law
mental_models.hint: With enough users, every observable behavior of a system will be depended on by somebody.

mental_models.name: Brooks's Law
mental_models.hint: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later due to communication overhead.

mental_models.name: Postel's Law (Robustness Principle)
mental_models.hint: Be conservative in what you send, and liberal in what you accept from others.

mental_models.name: Amdahl's Law
mental_models.hint: The overall performance improvement of a system is strictly limited by its slowest non-parallelizable component.

mental_models.name: Antifragility (Taleb)
mental_models.hint: Things that benefit and grow stronger from disorder, volatility, stressors, and random shocks.

mental_models.name: Ergodicity
mental_models.hint: When the average outcome of a group over time equals the average outcome of an individual over time.

mental_models.name: Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety
mental_models.hint: If a system is to survive, the variety of its control mechanisms must equal or exceed the variety of disturbances.

mental_models.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
mental_models.hint: When a system in equilibrium is subjected to change, it adjusts to counteract the imposed change.

mental_models.name: Tragedy of the Commons
mental_models.hint: Individual users acting independently deplete a shared, unowned resource contrary to common good.

mental_models.name: Red Queen Effect
mental_models.hint: You must continuously adapt and evolve merely to maintain your current competitive position.

mental_models.name: Power Laws & Fat Tails
mental_models.hint: A tiny fraction of events or inputs generate the overwhelming majority of total outcomes.

mental_models.name: Normal Accidents (Perrow)
mental_models.hint: In complex, tightly-coupled systems, catastrophic failures are inevitable structural events, not user errors.

mental_models.name: Gresham's Law
mental_models.hint: Bad money, standards, or incentives drive out good ones when forced to circulate at equal value.

mental_models.name: Pournelle's Law of Bureaucracy
mental_models.hint: In any bureaucracy, people dedicated to the organization's goals are controlled by those dedicated to the bureaucracy itself.

mental_models.name: Skin in the Game
mental_models.hint: People who make decisions must share in the downside risk of bad outcomes to ensure sound decisions.

mental_models.name: Via Negativa
mental_models.hint: Improving systems by subtracting errors, risks, and bad habits rather than adding complexity.

mental_models.name: Comparative Advantage
mental_models.hint: Maximizing total output by specializing in tasks where your opportunity cost is lowest.

mental_models.name: Opportunity Cost
mental_models.hint: The true cost of any decision is the value of the next best alternative you sacrificed.

mental_models.name: Theory of Constraints (Goldratt)
mental_models.hint: A system's total throughput is governed entirely by a single primary bottleneck.

mental_models.name: Feedback Loops (Positive vs Negative)
mental_models.hint: Negative feedback loops restore stability; positive feedback loops drive exponential divergence or collapse.

mental_models.name: Sayre's Law
mental_models.hint: In any dispute, the intensity of feeling is inversely proportional to the importance of the issue.

mental_models.name: Shirky Principle
mental_models.hint: Institutions will try to preserve the problem to which they are the solution.

mental_models.name: Local vs Global Optimum
mental_models.hint: Optimizing individual components in isolation frequently prevents the entire system from reaching its global peak.

mental_models.name: Margin of Safety
mental_models.hint: Building buffer capacity into designs and estimates to survive unexpected shocks and miscalculations.

mental_models.name: Sturgeon's Law
mental_models.hint: Ninety percent of everything is low quality; focus your search ruthlessly on the ten percent that matters.

mental_models.name: Two-Way vs One-Way Doors
mental_models.hint: Reversible decisions should be made quickly with limited data; irreversible decisions require deep deliberation.

mental_models.name: Campbell's Law
mental_models.hint: The more any quantitative social indicator is used for decision-making, the more subject it will be to corruptive pressures.

mental_models.name: Coordination Traps
mental_models.hint: Situations where everyone wants a better equilibrium, but no single participant can move without suffering alone.

mental_models.name: Schelling Points
mental_models.hint: Solutions that people tend to converge on by default in the absence of explicit communication.

mental_models.name: Principal-Agent Problem
mental_models.hint: Conflicts of interest that arise when one person is authorized to make decisions on behalf of another.

mental_models.name: Information Asymmetry
mental_models.hint: Transactions where one party possesses superior information, creating adverse selection and market decay.

mental_models.name: Tit-for-Tat Strategy
mental_models.hint: Cooperate on the first move, then simply mirror your opponent's previous move: simple, forgiving, and undefeated.

mental_models.name: Winner's Curse
mental_models.hint: The winning bidder in an auction with incomplete information typically overpays by exceeding intrinsic value.

mental_models.name: Costly Signaling
mental_models.hint: Signals are only credible if they require a prohibitive expenditure of resources that impostors cannot fake.

mental_models.name: Tragedy of the Anticommons
mental_models.hint: When too many distinct rights-holders can block one another, valuable resources remain completely unused.

mental_models.name: Mechanism Design
mental_models.hint: Designing the rules of a game so that players' self-interested actions naturally yield the desired social outcome.

mental_models.name: The Pareto Principle
mental_models.hint: Roughly 80 percent of consequences originate from 20 percent of causes.

mental_models.name: Dunbar's Number
mental_models.hint: The cognitive limit to the number of stable social relationships an individual can maintain is around 150.

mental_models.name: Metcalfe's Law
mental_models.hint: The value of a telecommunications network is proportional to the square of the number of connected users.

mental_models.name: Jevons Paradox
mental_models.hint: Technological improvements that increase efficiency in using a resource tend to increase total consumption of it.

paradoxes.name: Braess's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Adding capacity to a network can reduce overall throughput when individual actors choose selfish shortcuts.

paradoxes.name: Simpson's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A trend that appears in several distinct groups disappears or reverses when the groups are combined.

paradoxes.name: The Monty Hall Problem
paradoxes.hint: Switching doors doubles your winning probability from one-third to two-thirds due to conditional probability.

paradoxes.name: The Birthday Paradox
paradoxes.hint: In a room of just 23 people, there is a 50 percent chance that two share the exact same birthday.

paradoxes.name: The Fermi Paradox
paradoxes.hint: If intelligent extraterrestrial life is statistically probable, why is observable evidence completely absent?

paradoxes.name: Ship of Theseus
paradoxes.hint: If every original component of an object is replaced over time, does its fundamental identity persist?

paradoxes.name: The Mpemba Effect
paradoxes.hint: Under specific thermodynamic conditions, warmer water can freeze faster than colder water.

paradoxes.name: Berkson's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Two completely independent traits appear negatively correlated because of how the sample was selected.

paradoxes.name: The Inspection Paradox
paradoxes.hint: You will wait longer than the average bus interval because longer intervals are more likely to be arrived at.

paradoxes.name: Parrondo's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Combining two losing games alternately according to a specific rule can result in a winning game.

paradoxes.name: The Coastline Paradox
paradoxes.hint: The measured perimeter of a landmass increases indefinitely as your measuring unit becomes smaller.

paradoxes.name: Paradox of Thrift
paradoxes.hint: If every household saves more money during a recession, aggregate demand collapses, lowering total savings.

paradoxes.name: Paradox of Tolerance
paradoxes.hint: Unlimited tolerance must inevitably lead to the disappearance of tolerance if intolerant forces are tolerated.

paradoxes.name: Paradox of Choice
paradoxes.hint: An abundance of options increases anxiety, paralysis, and post-decision regret rather than satisfaction.

paradoxes.name: Sorites Paradox
paradoxes.hint: If removing one grain of sand does not turn a heap into a non-heap, at what point does it cease being a heap?

paradoxes.name: Newcomb's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A decision dilemma between free will and an infallible predictor who anticipates your choice.

paradoxes.name: Allais Paradox
paradoxes.hint: People systematically violate expected utility theory when choices involve certainty versus high probability.

paradoxes.name: St. Petersburg Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A lottery with infinite expected monetary value that rational participants will only pay a small fee to play.

paradoxes.name: Moravec's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: High-level reasoning requires very little computation, while low-level sensory-motor skills require enormous computation.

paradoxes.name: The Abilene Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A group collectively decides on an action that counteracts the actual preferences of every individual member.

paradoxes.name: Polanyi's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: We know more than we can tell: human tacit knowledge cannot be fully codified into explicit rules.

paradoxes.name: The Friendship Paradox
paradoxes.hint: On average, your friends have more friends than you do, due to network sampling bias.

paradoxes.name: Peto's Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Incidence of cancer does not correlate with the number of cells in an organism across species (e.g. whales vs humans).

paradoxes.name: Arrow's Impossibility Theorem
paradoxes.hint: No ranked-choice voting system can satisfy a set of basic fair criteria simultaneously.

paradoxes.name: Russell's Barber Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A barber shaves all men who do not shave themselves: does the barber shave himself?

paradoxes.name: Crocodile Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A crocodile promises to return a child if the father correctly predicts what the crocodile will do.

paradoxes.name: Raven Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Observing a green apple provides logical inductive evidence that all ravens are black.

paradoxes.name: Unexpected Hanging Paradox
paradoxes.hint: A prisoner is told an execution will occur on an unexpected day next week, which logic seems to rule impossible.

paradoxes.name: Paradox of Value (Diamond-Water)
paradoxes.hint: Water is essential for all life but cheap, while diamonds are completely non-essential but vastly expensive.

paradoxes.name: Catch-22
paradoxes.hint: A problematic situation for which the only solution is denied by a rule inherent in the problem.

paradoxes.name: Hedonistic Paradox
paradoxes.hint: Constant, deliberate pursuit of pleasure is the quickest way to guarantee misery and dissatisfaction.

paradoxes.name: Benford's Law
paradoxes.hint: In naturally occurring numerical datasets, the digit 1 appears as the leading digit over 30 percent of the time.

paradoxes.name: Turing Halting Problem
paradoxes.hint: It is mathematically impossible to write a general algorithm that determines whether any arbitrary program halts.

paradoxes.name: Gott's Delta t Argument
paradoxes.hint: Predicting the future longevity of an ongoing phenomenon based only on assuming you are observing it at a random point.

paradoxes.name: Liar Paradox
paradoxes.hint: The statement 'This statement is false' cannot be consistently assigned truth or falsehood.

thought_experiments.name: The Experience Machine (Nozick)
thought_experiments.hint: If a supercomputer could stimulate your brain to experience any fantasy for life, would you plug in permanently?

thought_experiments.name: Mary the Color Scientist (Jackson)
thought_experiments.hint: A neuroscientist knows every physical fact about color from a monochrome room. Does she learn anything when seeing red?

thought_experiments.name: The Chinese Room (Searle)
thought_experiments.hint: A person translates Chinese characters using mechanical rulebooks without understanding a single word.

thought_experiments.name: The Invisible Gorilla (Simons & Chabris)
thought_experiments.hint: When focusing intensely on a counting task, people systematically miss an obvious gorilla walking across the frame.

thought_experiments.name: The Trolley Problem
thought_experiments.hint: Diverting a runaway trolley to save five people by killing one: utilitarian outcome versus active deontological harm.

thought_experiments.name: Parfit's Teletransporter Paradox
thought_experiments.hint: A machine scans your atoms, destroys your original body, and builds an identical duplicate on Mars. Did you survive?

thought_experiments.name: Rawls's Veil of Ignorance
thought_experiments.hint: Designing a just society without knowing your own wealth, talent, gender, or social position in advance.

thought_experiments.name: Schrödinger's Cat
thought_experiments.hint: A cat in a sealed box with radioactive decay exists simultaneously in a superposition of alive and dead until observed.

thought_experiments.name: Maxwell's Demon
thought_experiments.hint: A hypothetical creature sorting fast and slow molecules to violate the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

thought_experiments.name: Einstein's Light Beam Ride
thought_experiments.hint: Imagining racing alongside a light wave led directly to the formulation of special relativity.

thought_experiments.name: Brain in a Vat (Putnam)
thought_experiments.hint: Could you be a disembodied brain wired to a supercomputer simulating all sensory inputs?

thought_experiments.name: Laplace's Demon
thought_experiments.hint: An intellect that knows the precise position and momentum of every atom in the universe predicting all future events.

thought_experiments.name: Lucretius' Spear
thought_experiments.hint: If you stand at the edge of the universe and throw a spear, what happens? Space must be boundless.

thought_experiments.name: Buridan's Ass
thought_experiments.hint: A donkey placed equidistant between two identical piles of hay starves to death for lack of a reason to pick one.

thought_experiments.name: Swampman (Davidson)
thought_experiments.hint: Lightning obliterates a man and accidentally configures a molecule-for-molecule replica from swamp muck.

thought_experiments.name: The Prisoner's Dilemma
thought_experiments.hint: Two rational actors acting in pure self-interest produce an outcome worse than if they had cooperated.

thought_experiments.name: The Stag Hunt (Rousseau)
thought_experiments.hint: A dilemma between high-reward collective coordination (hunting a stag) and low-reward individual safety (hunting a hare).

thought_experiments.name: The Utility Monster (Nozick)
thought_experiments.hint: An entity that converts each unit of consumed resources into a thousand times more happiness than ordinary humans.

thought_experiments.name: The Ring of Gyges (Plato)
thought_experiments.hint: If a magical ring granted total invisibility and immunity from consequences, would any rational person remain moral?

thought_experiments.name: Galileo's Falling Bodies
thought_experiments.hint: Tying a light stone to a heavy stone shows that falling speed cannot depend on weight without logical contradiction.

thought_experiments.name: The Infinite Monkey Theorem
thought_experiments.hint: A monkey hitting keys randomly on a typewriter for an infinite amount of time will eventually type Hamlet.

thought_experiments.name: The Divided Brain Experiments
thought_experiments.hint: Severing the corpus callosum reveals two separate conscious streams operating inside a single human skull.

thought_experiments.name: Newton's Rotating Bucket
thought_experiments.hint: The curved surface of spinning water demonstrates that acceleration is absolute relative to space itself.

thought_experiments.name: Ship of Theseus in Motion
thought_experiments.hint: If you collect all discarded planks from Theseus's ship and build a second ship, which one is the original?

thought_experiments.name: The Experience of Qualia
thought_experiments.hint: Why does sensory processing feel like anything at all from the inside, rather than operating in dark computation?

quotes.name: Charlie Munger
quotes.hint: On avoiding obvious stupidity rather than seeking brilliant moves.

quotes.name: Marcus Aurelius
quotes.hint: On maintaining strict focus only on what lies inside your direct control.

quotes.name: Seneca
quotes.hint: On the brevity of life and avoiding the illusion of perpetual busyness.

quotes.name: Epictetus
quotes.hint: On recognizing that events cannot hurt you; only your interpretation of them can.

quotes.name: Lao Tzu
quotes.hint: On effortless action (Wu Wei) and avoiding rigid force in leadership.

quotes.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
quotes.hint: On questioning default dogmas and forging internal strength from adversity.

quotes.name: Richard Feynman
quotes.hint: On the first principle: you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.

quotes.name: Viktor Frankl
quotes.hint: On the space between stimulus and response, where human freedom resides.

quotes.name: Carl Jung
quotes.hint: On bringing unconscious behaviors into awareness before they rule your life as fate.

quotes.name: Alan Watts
quotes.hint: On presence and the futility of trying to smooth rough water with a flatiron.

quotes.name: Aristotle
quotes.hint: On excellence being an art won by training and habituation rather than single acts.

quotes.name: Confucius
quotes.hint: On the humility of admitting what you do not know as the foundation of true knowledge.

quotes.name: Claude Shannon
quotes.hint: On information as the reduction of uncertainty in a noisy world.

quotes.name: John von Neumann
quotes.hint: On truth and mathematical simplicity versus human intuition.

quotes.name: Blaise Pascal
quotes.hint: On human troubles originating from man's inability to sit quietly in a room alone.

quotes.name: Arthur Schopenhauer
quotes.hint: On talent hitting a target no one else can hit, while genius hits a target no one else can see.

quotes.name: Søren Kierkegaard
quotes.hint: On life only being understood backwards, while it must be lived forwards.

quotes.name: Ralph Waldo Emerson
quotes.hint: On self-reliance and the foolish consistency that hobbles little minds.

quotes.name: Michel de Montaigne
quotes.hint: On questioning convictions: 'What do I know?' and the virtue of intellectual doubt.

quotes.name: Heraclitus
quotes.hint: On perpetual flux: no man ever steps in the same river twice.

quotes.name: Sun Tzu
quotes.hint: On winning without conflict and understanding the terrain before engaging.

quotes.name: Baruch Spinoza
quotes.hint: On striving neither to weep nor to detest, but solely to understand.

quotes.name: William James
quotes.hint: On the art of being wise being the art of knowing what to overlook.

quotes.name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
quotes.hint: On the limits of my language meaning the limits of my world.

quotes.name: Bertrand Russell
quotes.hint: On the fundamental cause of trouble: the stupid are cocksure while the intelligent are full of doubt.

quotes.name: Leonardo da Vinci
quotes.hint: On simplicity being the ultimate sophistication.

quotes.name: Buckminster Fuller
quotes.hint: On changing things by building a new model that makes the existing model obsolete.

quotes.name: Alan Turing
quotes.hint: On machines taking us by surprise with immense regularity.

quotes.name: Niels Bohr
quotes.hint: On an expert being someone who has made all the mistakes that can be made in a narrow field.

quotes.name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
quotes.hint: On avoiding ruin: what matters is not how frequently you are right, but how much you lose when wrong.

facts.name: Ant Colony Optimization
facts.hint: Ants solve complex traveling-salesperson routing problems with zero central coordination via evaporating pheromones.

facts.name: Fungal Mycorrhizal Networks
facts.hint: Underground fungal superhighways allow trees to trade nutrients and distribute warning signals across miles.

facts.name: Superfluidity at Macro Scales
facts.hint: Liquid helium cooled near absolute zero loses all viscosity and climbs upward over container walls.

facts.name: Deep-Ocean Chemosynthesis
facts.hint: Ecosystems thriving around volcanic vents in total darkness relying on hydrogen sulfide rather than sunlight.

facts.name: Corvid Multi-Stage Tool Use
facts.hint: Crows and ravens solve novel eight-step mechanical puzzles and manufacture compound tools from scratch.

facts.name: Polynesian Star Navigation
facts.hint: Wayfinders sailed thousands of miles across the open Pacific using only wave swells, bird flight, and zenith stars.

facts.name: Tardigrade Cryptobiosis
facts.hint: Water bears survive vacuum, cosmic radiation, and absolute zero by suspending metabolism in dry vitrified glass.

facts.name: Cephalopod RNA Editing
facts.hint: Octopuses and squids dynamically recode their own RNA to fine-tune nervous system proteins for freezing waters.

facts.name: Slime Mold Railway Optimization
facts.hint: Physarum polycephalum recreates the exact Tokyo rail transit network topology when searching for oat flakes.

facts.name: Quantum Entanglement
facts.hint: Entangled quantum particles maintain coordinated states instantaneously across arbitrary light-years of distance.

facts.name: Avian Magnetoreception
facts.hint: Migratory birds use cryptochrome proteins in their retinas to literally see Earth's magnetic field lines.

facts.name: Bathypelagic Bioluminescence
facts.hint: Over 75 percent of deep-sea creatures generate their own cold light for camouflage, signaling, and hunting.

facts.name: Mantis Shrimp Vision
facts.hint: Mantis shrimp possess 16 distinct color photoreceptor channels and can perceive polarized and ultraviolet light.

facts.name: Acacia Tree Warning Signals
facts.hint: When browsed by herbivores, acacia trees release ethylene gas to warn neighboring trees to flood leaves with tannins.

facts.name: Prime Number Cicada Cycles
facts.hint: Periodical cicadas emerge every 13 or 17 years—prime numbers that prevent synchronization with predator life cycles.

facts.name: Venus Flytrap Counting Potential
facts.hint: The trap requires two trigger hair touches within 20 seconds to close, preventing wasted energy on falling debris.

facts.name: Whale Fall Oases
facts.hint: A single sunken whale carcass nourishes complex specialized deep-sea ecosystems for over a century.

facts.name: Bacterial Quorum Sensing
facts.hint: Bacteria coordinate group virulence and biofilm creation only after measuring chemical population density thresholds.

facts.name: Gecko Van der Waals Adhesion
facts.hint: Geckos cling to smooth vertical glass using billions of microscopic spatulae that bond via atomic intermolecular forces.

facts.name: Axolotl Regeneration
facts.hint: Axolotls can regrow complete limbs, spinal cords, heart muscle, and portions of their brain without scarring.

facts.name: The Pitch Drop Experiment
facts.hint: The world's longest running lab experiment shows that solid-looking pitch is actually an ultra-dense fluid dripping once a decade.

facts.name: Synchronous Firefly Phase Locking
facts.hint: Thousands of fireflies along riverbanks synchronize flashes into unison through purely local mathematical phase adjustment.

facts.name: Euplectella Glass Sponge
facts.hint: Deep-sea glass sponges construct silica fiber lattices that surpass human fiber-optic cables in fracture resistance.

facts.name: Thermohaline Circulation Conveyor
facts.hint: A global oceanic conveyor belt driven by salt density and temperature circulates ocean waters over a 1,000-year cycle.

facts.name: Oklo Natural Nuclear Reactor
facts.hint: Two billion years ago in Gabon, natural uranium deposits and groundwater sustained self-regulating nuclear fission.

facts.name: Pando Aspen Root Organism
facts.hint: A 40,000-tree aspen forest in Utah sharing a single massive subterranean root system weighing 6,000 tons.

facts.name: Starling Murmuration Dynamics
facts.hint: Flocks of starlings execute instantaneous evasive aerial maneuvers with each bird reacting only to its seven closest neighbors.

facts.name: The Stroop Effect
facts.hint: The brain experiences severe reaction latency when the font color of a word conflicts with the written semantic color name.

facts.name: Sonoluminescence
facts.hint: Imploding gas bubbles in liquid subjected to acoustic sound waves reach temperatures hotter than the sun's surface and emit light.

facts.name: Honeybee Waggle Dance
facts.hint: Returning scout bees encode the exact distance, angle relative to the sun, and quality of food sources through figure-eight dances.

facts.name: Leafcutter Ant Agriculture
facts.hint: Ants cultivate fungal gardens underground using harvested leaves, protecting crops with symbiotic antibiotic-producing bacteria.

facts.name: Epigenetic Memory in Nematodes
facts.hint: Pathogen avoidance learning in C. elegans is passed down for four generations through small non-coding RNA inheritance.

facts.name: Tardigrade Radiation Resistance
facts.hint: A damage suppressor protein (Dsup) physically wraps around tardigrade DNA like a shield against ionizing radiation.

facts.name: Glass Wing Butterfly Nanostructures
facts.hint: Wings with irregular nanopillars that eliminate light reflection, making them completely transparent to predators.

facts.name: Immortal Jellyfish (Turritopsis)
facts.hint: When stressed or injured, cells revert via transdifferentiation back into polyp form, achieving biological immortality.
